channel.title: Religion News Service - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Religion News Service (religionnews.com)

item.title: What to know about the investigation into Catholic priests in Rhode Island and sexual abuse charges
item.description: PROVIDENCE, R.I. (AP) — The report was released by Rhode Island Attorney General Peter Neronha, whose office has been investigating the diocese since 2019.

item.title: Pakistan says its forces killed 67 Afghan troops in cross-border clashes. Kabul rejects the claim
item.description: The Taliban defense ministry in Kabul, the Afghan capital, rejected Pakistan’s claim. A ministry spokesman said Afghan forces in the past 24 hours repelled Pakistani attacks, destroying about a dozen military posts and killing four Pakistani soldiers.

item.title: From Karachi to Beirut, Khamenei’s death sends shockwaves across the Shiite world
item.description: Shiite Muslims make up around 10% to 15% of the world’s Muslim population, concentrated mainly in Iran, Iraq, Bahrain and Azerbaijan, while there are also significant communities in Pakistan, Lebanon and Yemen.

item.title: A son of Iran’s late supreme leader is a possible candidate to replace his father as war rages
item.description: A secretive figure within the Islamic Republic, Mojtaba Khamenei has not been seen publicly since Saturday, when the Israeli airstrike targeting the supreme leader's offices killed his 86-year-old father.

item.title: Turkey’s Erdogan offers to try to revive a truce as Pakistan-Afghan border clashes enter sixth day
item.description: The conflict erupted last week with Afghanistan launching attacks on Thursday in retaliation for Pakistani airstrikes the previous weekend.

item.title: Judge blocks DeSantis’ terrorist label of Muslim group
item.description: The court’s injunction allows CAIR-Florida to continue its work while the group’s lawsuit plays out.

item.title: When the bombs fall on other people’s children
item.description: If we cannot feel the death of an Iranian child with the same moral clarity as the death of a child in the United States, then something in us has been deformed.

item.title: The Western Wall isn’t just a public place — it’s an Orthodox synagogue
item.description: In the debate over Western Wall prayer, the traditional case deserves a hearing.

item.title: In Nigeria’s protracted violence, debate over whether religion is the cause, or the casualty
item.description: While many Christians see persecution, analysts and officials say the country’s long-running conflict is driven largely by insecurity, land disputes and criminal networks affecting both Muslims and Christians.

item.title: Beth Moore to end Living Proof events in 2027
item.description: selling author and longtime Bible teacher still plans to speak but will no longer host large-scale events.
